derivations.claim: Preliminary zero-extension claim. Let $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and vanish outside a compact $K\subseteq\Omega$. Then its zero extension $\widetilde h$ is continuous on $\mathbb R^4$: off $K$ it vanishes on the open set $\Omega\setminus K$ and is zero outside $\Omega$, while at any $x\in\partial K$ one has $h(x)=0$, because $h(x)\ne0$ would put a whole neighbourhood of $x$ inside $\{h\ne0\}\subseteq K$ and make $x$ interior to $K$. Hence $h=0$ on $\partial K$, and $\widetilde h$ is continuous and compactly supported with support contained in $K\subseteq\Omega$; by [F4] it is Riemann integrable on every box containing its support, so $\int_\Omega h\,d^4x$ is well defined and, by [F2], independent of the bounding box.
For (a), suppose $g(p)\ne0$ for some $p\in\Omega$.

For (b), let $K:=\operatorname{supp}f$, a compact subset of $\Omega$. By [F1] there is a box $Q$ with $K\subseteq\operatorname{int}Q$; write the chart coordinates as $(x^a,y)$ and $Q=[u_a,v_a]\times Q'$. For fixed $y\in Q'$ the function $t\mapsto f(t,y)g(t,y)$ is $C^1$ on $[u_a,v_a]$ as a function on that interval, with derivative $\partial_af(t,y)g(t,y)+f(t,y)\partial_ag(t,y)$ by [F8]; this derivative is continuous, hence integrable on $[u_a,v_a]$ by [F4]. Since $K\subseteq\operatorname{int}Q$, the points $(u_a,y)$ and $(v_a,y)$ lie outside $K$, so $f$ and hence $fg$ vanish at both endpoints.

For (c), fix $S>0$ with $[-S,S]\subseteq(-s_0,s_0)$ and a box $Q$ with $K\subseteq\operatorname{int}Q$, $K$ as in the hypothesis; write $Q=[u_a,v_a]\times Q'$ and define $H(s,y):=\int_{u_a}^{v_a}F(s;t,y)\,dt$ for $(s,y)\in[-S,S]\times Q'$. For each $s$ the function $z\mapsto F(s,z)$ is continuous on the box $Q$, hence integrable by [F4], and all its sections along the $a$-th coordinate are continuous, hence integrable; so [F6] gives $\int_QF(s,z)\,d^4z=\int_{Q'}H(s,y)\,dy$. Moreover $H$ is continuous on $[-S,S]\times Q'$, since $|H(s,y)-H(s_0,y_0)|\le(v_a-u_a)\sup_{t}|F(s;t,y)-F(s_0;t,y_0)|$ and $F$ is uniformly continuous on the compact box $[-S,S]\times Q$ by [F11].

For fixed $y\in Q'$, [F10] applied to $(s,t)\mapsto F(s;t,y)$ on $[-S,S]\times[u_a,v_a]$ shows that $s\mapsto H(s,y)$ is differentiable with $\partial_sH(s,y)=\int_{u_a}^{v_a}\partial_sF(s;t,y)\,dt$; then [F7] applied to $\tau\mapsto H(\tau,y)$ gives, for $s\ne s_0$, $$\frac{H(s,y)-H(s_0,y)}{s-s_0}=\frac1{s-s_0}\int_{s_0}^s\partial_sH(\tau,y)\,d\tau,\qquad \Big|\frac{H(s,y)-H(s_0,y)}{s-s_0}-\partial_sH(s_0,y)\Big|\le\sup_{\tau\in[s_0,s]}|\partial_sH(\tau,y)-\partial_sH(s_0,y)|.$$

Let $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and nonnegative, vanish outside a compact subset of $\Omega$, and satisfy $h\ge a>0$ on a nondegenerate closed box $Q_1\subseteq\Omega$. Choose a box $Q$ whose interior contains $\operatorname{supp}\widetilde h\cup Q_1$, and cut $Q$ successively along the coordinate hyperplanes carrying the faces of $Q_1$, so that $Q_1$ becomes one cell of a grid partition of $Q$. By step 1.1 and the additive splitting of [F3], together with monotonicity on the $Q_1$-cell and [F5], $$\int_\Omega h\,d^4x=\int_Q\widetilde h\ge\int_{Q_1}h\ge a\operatorname{vol}(Q_1)>0,$$ because $\widetilde h\ge0$ on $Q$.

In the situation of step 1.2, replacing $(g,\psi)$ by $(-g,-\psi)$ preserves the hypothesis and the conclusion, so assume $g(p)>0$. Continuity gives $\delta>0$ with $g>g(p)/2$ on the closed ball $\bar B_\delta(p)\subseteq\Omega$; choosing a nondegenerate closed box $Q_1$ with centre $p$ and all vertices in that ball gives $g\ge a:=g(p)/2>0$ on $Q_1$. Apply [F9] to the compact set $Q_1$ inside the open set $B_\delta(p)$ to obtain a smooth $\rho:\mathbb R^4\to[0,1]$ with $\rho=1$ on $Q_1$ and $\operatorname{supp}\rho\subseteq B_\delta(p)\subseteq\Omega$, and set $\psi:=\rho|_\Omega$. Then $\psi$ is smooth and compactly supported in $\Omega$, and by [F12] the product $g\psi$ is continuous, nonnegative on $\Omega$, supported in the compact set $\operatorname{supp}\psi\subseteq\Omega$, and equal to $g\ge a$ on $Q_1$.

For (b), both products $(\partial_af)g$ and $f(\partial_ag)$ are continuous on $\Omega$ and vanish outside $K=\operatorname{supp}f$; by step 1.1 their zero extensions are continuous and compactly supported, and by [F2] $$\int_\Omega(\partial_af)g\,d^4x=\int_Q(\partial_af)g\,d^4x,\qquad \int_\Omega f(\partial_ag)\,d^4x=\int_Qf(\partial_ag)\,d^4x.$$

For (c), the functions $z\mapsto F(s,z)$ and $z\mapsto\partial_sF(s,z)$ are, for each fixed $s\in[-S,S]$, continuous on $\Omega$ and vanish outside the compact $K$; by step 1.1 their zero extensions are continuous and compactly supported, and by [F2] $$\int_\Omega F(s,z)\,d^4z=\int_QF(s,z)\,d^4z,\qquad \int_\Omega\partial_sF(s,z)\,d^4z=\int_Q\partial_sF(s,z)\,d^4z.$$
For every $y\in Q'$, [F7] applied to the function $t\mapsto f(t,y)g(t,y)$ of step 1.3 gives $$\int_{u_a}^{v_a}\big(\partial_af\,g+f\,\partial_ag\big)\,dt=(fg)(v_a,y)-(fg)(u_a,y)=0.$$

Let $\varepsilon>0$. The continuous $\partial_sF$ is uniformly continuous on the compact box $[-S,S]\times[u_a,v_a]\times Q'$ by [F11]; choose $\delta>0$ so that $|s-s_0|<\delta$ implies $|\partial_sF(\tau;t,y)-\partial_sF(s_0;t,y)|<\varepsilon$ for every $\tau$ between $s_0$ and $s$, every $t\in[u_a,v_a]$ and every $y\in Q'$. Then $|\partial_sH(\tau,y)-\partial_sH(s_0,y)|\le(v_a-u_a)\varepsilon$ for all such $\tau,y$, and step 1.5 gives $$\Big|\frac{H(s,y)-H(s_0,y)}{s-s_0}-\partial_sH(s_0,y)\Big|\le(v_a-u_a)\varepsilon\qquad(y\in Q').$$

By step 2.1 applied to the nonnegative continuous $h=g\psi$ of step 2.2, $\int_\Omega g\psi\,d^4x\ge a\operatorname{vol}(Q_1)>0$, contradicting the hypothesis $\int_\Omega g\psi\,d^4x=0$. Hence $g(p)=0$ for every $p\in\Omega$, proving (a).

For (c), continuity of the derivative function: by [F4] the function $z\mapsto\partial_sF(s,z)$ is integrable on $Q$ for every $s$, and [F3] and [F5] give, for $s,s_0\in[-S,S]$, $$\Big|\int_Q\partial_sF(s,z)\,d^4z-\int_Q\partial_sF(s_0,z)\,d^4z\Big|\le\operatorname{vol}(Q)\sup_{z\in Q}|\partial_sF(s,z)-\partial_sF(s_0,z)|,$$ which tends to $0$ as $s\to s_0$ by the uniform continuity [F11] of $\partial_sF$ on the compact box $[-S,S]\times Q$. Hence $s\mapsto\int_\Omega\partial_sF(s,z)\,d^4z$ is continuous on $[-S,S]$ by step 2.4.

For (b), the integrands $(\partial_af)g$ and $f(\partial_ag)$ are continuous on the box $Q=[u_a,v_a]\times Q'$, hence integrable by [F4], and their sections along the $a$-th coordinate are continuous, hence integrable; by [F6] the box integrals equal the iterated integrals. Integrating the identity of step 2.5 over $Q'$ and using [F3] linearity gives $0=\int_Q(\partial_af)g\,d^4x+\int_Qf(\partial_ag)\,d^4x$, that is $\int_\Omega(\partial_af)g\,d^4x=-\int_\Omega f(\partial_ag)\,d^4x$ by step 2.3. This proves (b).

For (c), let $G(s):=\int_\Omega F(s,z)\,d^4z$. By steps 2.4 and 1.4, $G(s)=\int_{Q'}H(s,y)\,dy$ for $s\in[-S,S]$. For $s\ne s_0$, linearity [F3] gives $\frac{G(s)-G(s_0)}{s-s_0}=\int_{Q'}\frac{H(s,y)-H(s_0,y)}{s-s_0}\,dy$; by step 2.6 the integrands converge to $\partial_sH(s_0,\cdot)$ uniformly on $Q'$ as $s\to s_0$, so [F3] (absolute-value estimate) and [F4] yield $\lim_{s\to s_0}\frac{G(s)-G(s_0)}{s-s_0}=\int_{Q'}\partial_sH(s_0,y)\,dy$. By step 1.5 and [F6] applied to the continuous $\partial_sF(s_0,\cdot)$ this equals $\int_Q\partial_sF(s_0,z)\,d^4z=\int_\Omega\partial_sF(s_0,z)\,d^4z$, the last equality by step 2.4. Thus $G$ is differentiable on $[-S,S]$ with derivative $s\mapsto\int_\Omega\partial_sF(s,z)\,d^4z$, which is continuous by step 3.2; hence $G$ is $C^1$ on $[-S,S]$. Since every $s\in(-s_0,s_0)$ lies in some such $[-S,S]$, the map $s\mapsto\int_\Omega F(s,z)\,d^4z$ is $C^1$ on $(-s_0,s_0)$ with the stated derivative, proving (c).

derivations.claim: Fix a smooth compactly supported $h$. For every real $s$ and every $z\in\Omega$ set $\Phi_s(z):=L(\varphi+sh)(z)-L(\varphi)(z)$ and $F(s,z):=-(K/c)\Phi_s(z)$. Both $\Phi_s$ and $\partial_s\Phi_s$ are continuous on $\mathbb R\times\Omega$: each is a finite sum of products of the continuous maps $(s,z)\mapsto\partial_a\varphi(z)$, $(s,z)\mapsto\partial_ah(z)$, $(s,z)\mapsto h(z)$, $(s,z)\mapsto s$, $(s,z)\mapsto\varphi(z)+sh(z)$ and of the composites of the last of these with the continuous one-variable functions $V$ and $V'$, and [F7] gives continuity of all these sums, products and composites; both functions also vanish at every $z\notin\operatorname{supp}h$, because $\varphi+sh=\varphi$ there.

Apply [F1] to $F$ on $(-1,1)\times\Omega$: the relative action $S_h(s)=-(K/c)\int_\Omega\Phi_s\,d^4x$ is $C^1$ on $(-1,1)$ with $S_h'(0)=-(K/c)\int_\Omega\partial_s\Phi_0\,d^4x=\delta S(\varphi)[h]$, using the value of $\partial_s\Phi_s$ at $s=0$ from step 1.1; the integrand of $S_h(s)$ is supported in $\operatorname{supp}h$ for every $s$, so $S_h(s)$ is a finite Riemann integral for every real $s$ and $S_h'(0)=\delta S(\varphi)[h]$.
